Upgrade Your Home With Carefully Planned Flooring Installation Solutions

New flooring can transform how a home looks and feels, but lasting results start beneath the surface. RT Signature Homes plans each installation around the subfloor, moisture, transitions, and how each room is used, so your new hardwood, luxury vinyl, laminate, or tile is prepared and installed to last.

Typical scope

  • Existing-floor and subfloor assessment
  • Hardwood installation and qualifying refinishing
  • LVP and laminate installation
  • Tile flooring and transition coordination
  • Preparation, protection, base details, and final care guidance

Why choose us

Why Choose Us for Our Flooring Installation Services

Start beneath the floor

A flooring installation problem usually starts underneath, so we assess the subfloor, flatness, and moisture before choosing a material or a direction.

Transitions planned

Transitions, edges, and adjacent finishes are planned, because the details at thresholds and walls are where floors most often look unfinished.

Matched to the room

Material is matched to the room and the traffic it carries, so the floor performs where resilience matters and shows warmth where it counts.

Transform Outdated Rooms With Modern Flooring Styles and Finishes

Flooring carries color, texture, and continuity through a home, so updating it can modernize a space instantly. The right styles and finishes refresh outdated rooms while tying your interior together.

Flooring & Finish Palette Ideas

These palettes explore how wood, luxury vinyl, tile, and finishes can work together to bring a fresh, cohesive look across connected spaces.

Explore the gallery

Hardwood

Install Hardwood Flooring for Timeless Appeal and Lasting Performance

Hardwood brings warmth and timeless appeal to a home, and a lasting installation depends on the substrate, moisture, acclimation, and layout being planned before the first board goes down.

We plan species, grade, direction, and transitions to adjacent rooms, and where existing wood floors qualify, refinishing can restore them instead of replacing them.

LVP and laminate

Explore Luxury Vinyl Flooring for Versatile and Practical Interiors

Luxury vinyl and laminate are versatile, practical choices for busy households, standing up to moisture and traffic while offering a wide range of wood and stone looks.

Product construction, substrate tolerances, expansion requirements, and transitions all affect the result, so materials are matched to each room rather than chosen on appearance alone.

Tile and refinishing

Resolve flatness, layout, edges, and adjacent finishes.

Tile flooring needs appropriate substrate preparation, movement accommodation, layout, grout, and transition details.

Refinishing requires dust-control planning, finish selection, cure time, and realistic expectations for existing damage.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Project size, layout changes, and finish level
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, and project sequencing

Questions homeowners ask

Flooring Installation & Refinishing FAQs

How do I choose the right flooring for rooms with different needs?

Consider moisture exposure, foot traffic, cleaning requirements, comfort, and the room's overall design. Porcelain tile may suit bathrooms, while luxury vinyl or engineered wood may work well in living areas. Choosing materials based on each room's conditions helps balance appearance and performance.

Does existing flooring need to be removed before new flooring installation?

Not always. The decision depends on the existing material, its condition, the new flooring manufacturer's requirements, and the available floor height. Damaged flooring, loose materials, or unsuitable surfaces may need removal before installation can proceed properly.

What should be checked before installing new flooring over a concrete subfloor?

The concrete should be assessed for moisture, cracks, uneven areas, and surface contaminants. Moisture testing and appropriate preparation are especially important for wood-based and some resilient flooring products because excess moisture can contribute to warping, adhesive failure, or other installation problems.

Can I install the same flooring throughout my kitchen, living room, and hallway?

Yes, using the same flooring across connected areas can create a more continuous appearance and make smaller spaces feel more unified. However, the selected material must be suitable for each area's moisture exposure, traffic, and cleaning needs, with transitions planned where necessary.

Why can newly installed flooring develop gaps, lifting, or uneven areas?

These problems may result from an uneven subfloor, inadequate expansion gaps, moisture changes, unsuitable adhesives, or incorrect installation methods. Following manufacturer requirements and preparing the subfloor properly helps reduce these risks and supports a more stable finished floor.
